items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1959-09-01
items.q: King Oliver was gone. Johnny Dots was gone. I met them in Chicago.

ctx.x: The district. Oh hell yeah man. You was. I was playing with a fellow and Ken Beard in the daytime. Cans of the women, you know, the whole hustle of them. 10 cents a can and every night I'd get up there and play the blues with the piano player. Now he, I forget his name, he died. He was a sickly fellow but he died. But I, nothing but blues all night. I'd sit up and play the blues all night. A fellow named Tootlum. Tootlum. Gravity and Gravy. All right let me ask you this. It's known that Jelly Roll played here in…
Which band was it that Keppert was in you were in?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1958-05-24
items.q: well, I thought about Johnny Ducks. Always did.

ctx.x: Lewis is my favorite. Yeah. Always was. And the boy that I admire a lot now is Dave, Buddy Petit. That's the fellow I really did admire last year. And come to Plan Epsom thing, well, I thought about Johnny Ducks. Always did. You know, got to tell the truth about it.
Well, when you were young, who was your favorite trumpet player when you were a kid?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1957-multiple
items.q: So, Ori and Johnny Dotson, him. So, they invited me up to play a piece, and I played a piece

ctx.x: You remember some of the other good musicians around here? You said you played in Jack Carey's band. Who were some of the other bands, the other trumpet players you heard when you first came here?

When I first came here? Yeah. Well, Buddy Petit was one of the fellas, Ray and Plinistain. And Kid René. And Louis too, Louis Armstrong. He was cracking them up. But the idea about Louis, he always played off like the Capitol Boat. And going off something, you know, like that. He'd play in brass bands every now and then, but he wasn't exactly with us, because he always looked like a little above that, or some kind of really. Yeah. Big time people would hire him all the time, you know. He'd work with a kid, Ori,…
Louis thought you meant it though, huh, did he? Yeah. Louis thought they were going to hire you in this place?

items.title: Ernest "Punch" Miller Interview, 1971-04-08
items.q: the first people I saw was playing at the 25, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, and Bob Lyons on bass

ctx.x: since you're both sick right now.

Well, about me and Louis, I'll tell you about that. Uh... I left the country in 1918, and I was 18 years old. I went to World War I, and when I came back, the first people I saw was playing at the 25, Louis Armstrong, Kid Ory, Johnny Dots, Baby Dots, and Bob Lyons on bass, and Lorenzo Starrs on guitar, so... You had to play in a drum?
